articles.text:
Systems Planning And Analysis Receives Up To $55.7 Million Navy Trident II Support Order
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 10:45 AM
Systems Planning And Analysis Receives Up To $55.7 Million Navy Trident II Support Order
Systems Planning and Analysis has received a Navy task order valued at up to approximately $55.7 million to support the Trident II Strategic Weapons System.
The Alexandria, Virginia-based company will perform technical assessments and studies, systems engineering and analysis, program integration, and schedule support.
The cost-plus-fixed-fee term task order is identified as N0003027F3024. Its $55.7 million stated value includes optional line items, meaning the full amount depends on whether the Navy exercises those options.
Work is expected to continue through September 30, 2031. Washington, D.C., will account for 60% of performance, while Alexandria will account for 32%.
The remaining work will be distributed among Bangor, Washington; Denver, Colorado; Titusville, Florida; Kings Bay, Georgia; Pittsfield, Massachusetts; Valley Forge, Pennsylvania; Magna, Utah; and Sunnyvale, California. Each location represents 1% of performance.
Initial obligations total approximately $1.7 million. This includes $200,981 in fiscal 2026 research, development, test, and evaluation funding; $150,000 in fiscal 2027 RDT&E funding; and approximately $1.3 million in fiscal 2027 Navy operation and maintenance funding.
The $200,981 fiscal 2026 RDT&E allocation will expire at the end of fiscal 2027. The source announcement does not state that the remaining potential task-order value has been obligated.
The effort also benefits a foreign military sale to the United Kingdom, reflecting the U.K.’s role in the Trident strategic weapons enterprise.
The task order will be issued as a sole-source acquisition under an authority associated with federal small-business research and development programs.
Portfolio Acquisition Executive, Strategic Systems Programs in Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity. Strategic Systems Programs manages the Navy’s sea-based strategic deterrence systems.

articles.snippet:
Charta Health has raised $55 million in Series B funding to expand its artificial intelligence platform for medical chart review and create a common standard of billing accuracy for healthcare providers and insurers. Insight Partners led the round, with participation from existing investors Madrona, Bain Capital Ventures, and South Park Commons, along with QuantumLight.

articles.text:
Charta Health: $55 Million Series B To Expand AI Medical Chart Review
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 11, 2026
Charta Health: $55 Million Series B To Expand AI Medical Chart Review
Charta Health has raised $55 million in Series B funding to expand its artificial intelligence platform for medical chart review and create a common standard of billing accuracy for healthcare providers and insurers. Insight Partners led the round, with participation from existing investors Madrona, Bain Capital Ventures, and South Park Commons, along with QuantumLight.
Charta applies AI to unstructured clinical information, including physician notes, scanned orders, laboratory results, and images. Its technology reviews medical records to determine whether documented care supports the codes used for billing.
The company wants providers and payers to resolve coding discrepancies before a claim is submitted rather than through denials, audits, and appeals. Those administrative processes contribute billions of dollars in costs to the U.S. healthcare system.
Charta for Providers reviews every chart before billing and checks the documentation against official coding guidance, payer rules, and an organization’s clinical protocols. Findings are presented within electronic health record workflows for human approval.
The company says its platform produces consistent double-digit reductions in denial rates. It also gives compliance and medical leadership teams information about documentation gaps, recurring errors, and provider performance.
Charta works with healthcare organizations including American Family Care, Grow Therapy, and Pediatric Associates Family of Companies. It will use the funding to improve the accuracy and intelligence of its provider technology and expand into additional medical specialties.
The financing also supports Charta for Payers, a suite developed with one of the country’s largest health insurers. The offering initially focuses on Medicare Advantage and Affordable Care Act Marketplace plans.
Its six products cover retrospective hierarchical condition category coding, automated second-pass reviews, coder workflows, prospective risk-adjustment intelligence, audit preparation, and quality care-gap detection.
The technology can identify conditions documented but not coded and diagnoses that lack sufficient clinical support. Charta’s longer-term objective is to give providers and insurers a consistent interpretation of the same medical record before reimbursement decisions are made.
KEY QUOTE:
“Healthcare payments depend on the medical chart, and charting errors cause costly problems across the entire process. As payers and providers both adopt AI, we believe the opportunity lies in getting the underlying record, or the ‘ground truth,’ right before a claim is submitted. Charta pairs AI with customer-specific coding expertise and serves both sides of that market. We are excited to partner with Justin, Scott, and the team as they scale.”
Jeff Horing, Co-Founder and Managing Director at Insight Partners

articles.title: BITS Pilani raises USD 54 million through endowment drive in 23 months: Group VC V Ramgopal Rao
articles.snippet: BITS Pilani raises USD 54 million through endowment drive in 23 months: Group VC V Ramgopal Rao The Indian Express
articles.text:
BITS Pilani’s endowment fund has crossed USD 54 million, just 23 months after it set a target of USD 100 million, according to group Vice Chancellor V Ramgopal Rao.
While more than 24 individual alumni and alumni batches have each pledged USD one million or more, annual alumni giving reached a record Rs 82 crore in the financial year 2025 to 2026, a 43 per cent increase over the previous year and nearly 90 times the level recorded when the Alumni Relations Office was established in the financial year 2017 to 2018.
“Cumulative alumni contributions of Rs 256 crore have supported initiatives across BITS campuses. Founders, CEOs, scientists, reunion batches and companies led by alumni have contributed from India and around the world. When we set out to build a USD 100 million endowment, it was an ambitious goal. Our alumni have responded with extraordinary generosity,” Rao told.

articles.title: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM
articles.snippet: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM TechCrunch
articles.text:
Dreamteam , a startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with its AI-native CRM, betting that AI can finally shake up a market where established players have so far proved difficult to dislodge.
The funding comprises seed and Series A rounds, led by Together Fund and Accel respectively, with participation from Premji Invest. The San Francisco-based startup declined to disclose the size of each round or its valuation.
Traditional CRMs depend on salespeople to manually record customer interactions and keep deal information up to date. That often leaves businesses with incomplete or outdated information. Dreamteam aims to eliminate much of that work by automatically capturing context from sources including emails and customer conversations. It also uses AI agents to handle tasks such as follow-ups, meeting preparation, and pipeline monitoring.
Dreamteam co-founder and CEO Anand Venkatraman (pictured above, right) told TechCrunch that he had repeatedly encountered problems with traditional CRM platforms over more than 25 years in enterprise software, including at Salesforce and Freshworks. Salespeople spent considerable time updating records, yet managers still struggled to get a reliable picture of their business. “In all these years, I have never come across an instance where I could click a button and get a forecast from the CRM,” he said.
That experience led Venkatraman to co-found Dreamteam in 2025 with Senthil Kanthaswamy (pictured above, center), who spent more than nine years at Freshworks, most recently as a product leader at Freshservice, and Ramesh Parthasarathy (pictured above, left), who previously worked on AI and platform engineering at Freshworks.
At the heart of Dreamteam’s CRM is what it calls the Company Brain. This acts as virtual memory, pulling together information from emails, meetings, and other customer interactions to build a shared record of customer relationships. Four built-in AI agents use that information to research prospects, draft follow-up emails, flag potential risks to deals, and configure CRM workflows, with sales teams retaining control over what gets sent to customers.
Dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries in the three months since it began actively selling its product, with most paying for the service, Venkatraman said. The startup has also replaced established CRM platforms at several businesses, including Salesforce at healthcare company DMS Health and HubSpot at other customers.
The advertising sales team at media streaming company Plex also chose Dreamteam over HubSpot and other AI-native CRM alternatives, Venkatraman told TechCrunch. Plex’s co-founder and chief product officer Scott Olechowski said Dreamteam’s ability to integrate with AI tools already used across the company was a “game changer.”
Replacing established CRM platforms at scale may prove more difficult. In a blog post earlier this year, venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) argued that while AI could transform how businesses manage customer relationships, existing CRMs are likely to remain the systems where customer records are stored, with a new generation of AI-powered tools capturing much of the value by working on top of them.

articles.title: AI-Native CRM Dreamteam Raises $53 Million in Seed and Series A Funding
articles.snippet: AI-Native CRM Dreamteam Raises $53 Million in Seed and Series A Funding Wowtale
articles.text:
For more than two decades, CRMs such as Salesforce and HubSpot have depended on salespeople remembering to type in what happened on a call. When they forget, customer context disappears and the pipeline fills with stale data. Dreamteam , an AI-native CRM built on the opposite premise, said it raised $53 million from Accel, Together Fund and Premji Invest. The company described the amount as seed and Series A funding combined and did not disclose a valuation.
A CRM that fills itself from conversations
At the center of Dreamteam is what it calls the Company Brain, a running memory built from customer conversations, emails, meetings and workflows. It pulls out buyer intent, objections, competitor mentions and stakeholder dynamics. The company argues that legacy CRMs, built around structured fields and hand-coded workflows, cannot hold signals like a prospect hesitating on price or a board suddenly scrutinizing costs. It says an account that changes hands carries over the customer’s goals, objections and open commitments.
Four AI teammates work on top of that memory. Rachel is a research assistant that enriches accounts and contacts. Sally, the sales assistant, preps meetings, drafts follow-up emails and manages tasks. Raj is a RevOps partner that monitors the pipeline, flags at-risk deals and improves forecasts. Alex is a CRM administrator that configures the system from plain-language requests. The company says customers do not have to build or train their own agents.
Humans keep control. A person has to approve any outgoing email, teams set pricing rules and approval limits, and users can see where a recommendation came from and correct what the system remembers. Alongside the human interface, Dreamteam offers an API and a Model Context Protocol server so AI agents such as Claude or ChatGPT can reach the CRM. A feature called Magic Apps lets business users build apps and dashboards in natural language.
The company says more than 100 companies in 13 countries use it, and its press release puts the figure at hundreds across AI, online media, healthcare, manufacturing and consulting. Named customers include invideo, Plex and DMS Health. invideo started with a small pilot and expanded to its whole sales team, and Plex’s co-founder and chief product officer called its compatibility with existing AI tools like Claude “a game changer.” Revenue and pricing were not disclosed.
Three former Freshworks executives
The co-founders are former senior executives at Freshworks. CEO Anand Venkatraman leads sales and go-to-market, Ramesh Parthasarathy leads engineering and Senthil Kanthaswamy leads product. The company says they helped scale Freshworks from its early startup days through its IPO and have built AI applications since the GPT-2 era, scaling them to tens of thousands of businesses. When AI reasoning made it possible for software to understand context and carry out work, they decided to rebuild CRM from scratch rather than layer AI onto existing systems. Dreamteam was founded in 2025 and says it is headquartered in Sacramento, California.
Its blog post names Together Fund and Accel as leads, with Premji Invest participating. Together Fund, founded by Freshworks founder Girish Mathrubootham, is Dreamteam’s first institutional investor. Mathrubootham said the cloud wave created a generation of enterprise software leaders 25 years ago and that AI demands software rebuilt from the ground up, with CRM among the largest categories ripe for disruption
